legal_citations.title: Article 4: Consumer Rights
legal_citations.text: All prescribed obligations are consumer rights, including: obtaining true information on the commodities or service; protecting consumers' privacy and data security and not using these for promotion; fair and quick settlement for consumers' disputes; and obtaining fair compensation for damages caused to them or their property as a result of purchasing or using the commodity or receiving the service.

legal_citations.title: Article 10: Obligations of the Provider in Honouring the Warranty
legal_citations.text: The provider shall honour all warranties, provide spare parts and maintenance, replace the commodity or return its cash value, and be committed to after-sales service during the period specified. The provider shall guarantee the service is free from defects and flaws; otherwise it shall return the amount paid by the consumer or part thereof, or correctly re-provide the service.

legal_citations.title: Article 25: E-Commerce
legal_citations.text: E-commerce providers registered within the State shall provide consumers and competent authorities with their names, legal statuses, addresses, licensing authorities and sufficient information in Arabic on the provided commodity or service, its specifications, terms of contracting, payment and warranty.

legal_citations.title: Article 12: Flaw in the Commodity or Service
legal_citations.text: In case of discovering a flaw in the commodity or service, the provider shall repair, replace or recover the commodity and reimburse its price, or re-provide the service without charge, as prescribed by the Executive Regulation.
